correctness.rationale: For every path size and characteristic-two field, the n simple-root vectors form a basis of the zero-sum hyperplane; each affine local neighbor-parity update is an adjacent coordinate swap plus root translation. Every permutation sweep has a single (n+1)-cycle as linear part. Translation places it on a constant-sum affine hyperplane, and the path-adjacency kernel gives the exact alternating-index fixed-point obstruction. Counting g equal-value coordinate cycles proves the full fixed-count law, with explicit constructive primitive-period support and Möbius orbit inversion. The proof is all-size; the packaged verifier independently checked 4,696 full offset/order cases covering 154,528 configurations, plus 936 seeded checks.

value.rationale: The open path with sequential nearest-neighbor parity and static local forcing is a canonical natural finite dynamical model. An exact family-wide result is obtained for all field sizes, offsets and vertex orders, not arbitrary parameter slices: a single alternating forcing invariant sharply removes all periods lacking the full 2-adic divisor, and for power-of-two path lengths all configurations can be forced into maximal-length cycles. Complete orbit counts allow exact comparisons among forcing patterns and schedules.
